chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabie al-Musally, from Ahmad ibn Razin, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
‘Upon you is with the vinegar of wine, so immerse (in it), for there would not remain in your belly any insect but it would kill it’.
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of consuming wine vinegar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes vinegar derived from wine (*khal al-khamr*) as a potent vermifuge, asserting its ability to eradicate all internal parasites. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of utilizing accessible, natural remedies for gastrointestinal health, emphasizing the practical application of prophetic medicine (*al-tibb al-nabawi*) in daily life. The specificity of using wine-derived vinegar highlights the nuanced understanding of fermentation processes in classical Islamic medicine.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Rabie Al Musally, form Ahmad Bin Razeyn, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Upon you is with (eating) the wine vinegar, therefore immerse (bread etc.) in it, for there would not remain an insect in your inside but it would kill it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Rabi’ al-Musliy from Ahmad ibn Razin from Sufyan al-Simt who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must eat vinegar of wine and immerse (the morsel or use it very often) in it, because it does not leave any dawab (insects) animal in your belly without killing them.’”
